task: Upgrade system-generated experiment artifacts from Notes to capability-protected HTML Browser widgets backed by a versioned structured artifact store, while preserving legacy Notes and human-input behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: New setup, result, closed, and needs-input outputs create Browser widgets with exact workflow title markers, stable artifact URLs, canonical structured records, and durable connectors.
Artifact updates append versions and change rendered content without recreating the Browser widget.
The HTML renderer escapes all user/model content, rejects raw executable HTML, uses a strict CSP with same-origin assets, and remains responsive and keyboard accessible.
Capability reads use high-entropy opaque identifiers and constant-time token verification; revoked, guessed, unauthorized, and cross-canvas requests expose no artifact data.
Workflow detection accepts generated Browser widgets and legacy Notes while idea and human approval/review input remain Note-only.
Crash recovery reconciles persisted artifacts, Browser widgets, widget mappings, and connectors without duplicate effects.
Legacy generated Notes can be inventoried and mirrored idempotently in dry-run-first mode, with no deletion by default.
Both applications pass pytest, ruff, and mypy; security, large-payload, graph, restart, accessibility, and migration paths have regression coverage.
README, architecture, workflow, operations, standards, roadmap, changelog, and canonical use-case documentation describe the implemented service and deployment constraints.
blastRadius: workflow graph classification and loop scanning
contracts: Canvas Browser widgets are views and graph nodes; ArtifactStore is the canonical generated-artifact record.
Workflow title markers and connector semantics remain backward compatible.
Idea and human-authored control inputs remain Notes.
Capability URLs are bearer secrets and must not be logged or included in model/audit payloads.
Migration is dry-run/mirror-first, idempotent, and non-destructive by default.
Canvas remains workflow truth while the durable ledger owns artifact versions, mappings, recovery, and audit evidence.
